gap: No result ChatGPT got states that CKL's own US store sells a 2-PC, 2-monitor HDMI 2.1 KVM with EDID listed at 4K 144 Hz, the 922HUA-5, for $189. ChatGPT's high-refresh card, the TESmart HKS202-M24, costs $359 for the same 2×2 HDMI 2.1 job. At the 1-monitor tier, CKL's 62HUA-5 (HDMI 2.1, EDID, $129) costs the same as the HDMI 2.0, 4K 60 Hz TESmart HKS201-P23 that ChatGPT showed at $129.99.
standout_why: I compared five pages. dockgearhq.com/blog/best-kvm-switches-with-hdmi-2026 (Oct 13) gives no prices and names no CKL model; its only HDMI 2.1 pick with EDID is the 4-port TESmart HKS401-M23. thetechsearch.com (prices dated Oct 16) tops out at a TESmart dual 4K 60 Hz model for $199.99 and has no HDMI 2.1 tier. deskdna.com gives rough '~$' prices and sends high refresh to a DisplayPort TESmart (~$160). officekithq.com gives no prices and lists BENFEI, GREATHTEK, Jancane, UGREEN 75246 and IOGEAR. manbolo.com gives no prices and does not mention CKL or the TESmart M24 or EB23. No rival prices the HDMI 2.1 dual-monitor tier, and none compares CKL with TESmart.
decides: The basic 4K 60 Hz, 1-monitor pick stays the same, and the cheapest options are still around $30 to $48 (UGREEN on Amazon). Two picks change. (1) For 2 monitors at 4K 120 to 144 Hz over HDMI, the CKL 922HUA-5 at $189 does the core job for $170 less than ChatGPT's $359 TESmart. The TESmart keeps gigabit LAN sharing, front USB-C charging, a USB 3.0 hub and the VRR, ALLM and HDR features its listing names. CKL's listing only mentions sharing '1 more USB peripheral'. (2) For EDID on a budget, TESmart's own HKS201-EB23 has EDID emulation for $43.99. Two rivals say the UGREEN they pick either doesn't document EDID or doesn't support it. A shopper who reads 'EDID' in ChatGPT's checklist can get it for about $44. One trap needs flagging: CKL's 922HUA-4 ($169) is also listed as HDMI 2.1 4K 144 Hz, but its listing says 'does not support EDID emulation'.
